html:
"Anatolian tribes" is the map's label for the peoples of western and central Anatolia, today's Turkey, around 2000 BCE, before the Hittites united much of the land.

Several peoples lived here. The Hattians held the centre and gave their name to the land of Hatti. Speakers of Indo-European languages, among them the ancestors of the Hittites and the Luwians, lived alongside them. Most lived under small city kings.

Writing arrived with merchants: the Assyrian traders at Kanesh left thousands of clay tablets about the tin and cloth trade, and the local names in them are the first written record of these languages. On the west coast, Troy was a fortified town. Within a few centuries the Hittite kingdom had absorbed most of central Anatolia.
sum: "Anatolian tribes" is the map's label for the peoples of western and central Anatolia, today's Turkey, around 2000 BCE, before the Hittites united much of the land.
